title: Wilten Abbey Innsbruck
name: Wilten Abbey Innsbruck
kurzbeschreibung: The Premonstratensian Abbey of Stift Wilten at the foot of the Bergisel: Baroque monastery jewel founded in 1138 with collegiate basilica, museum, and Wiltener Sängerknaben.
beschreibung:
Overview

The historic Stift Wilten is situated in the southern Innsbruck district of the same name at the foot of the famous Bergisel at an altitude of approximately 590 metres. Founded in 1138 by Bishop Reginbert of Brixen and entrusted to the Premonstratensian Canons Regular, the abbey ranks among the most traditional and venerable spiritual centres in western Austria. The magnificently restored monastery complex is regarded as a masterpiece of Tyrolean Baroque and is famed worldwide as the home of the renowned Wiltener Sängerknaben – one of the oldest boys' choirs in the world.

Baroque Splendour & Giant Legend

Wilten's heritage reaches back to Roman antiquity, when the prominent Roman road station Veldidena flourished on this very site. According to the founding legend, the giant Haymon defeated the giant Thyrsus in fierce combat, founded the monastery out of deep remorse, and carried the heavy stone blocks with his own hands; two monumental statues of the giants continue to guard the abbey gate today. The Stiftskirche Wilten impresses with its breathtaking interior: masterly ceiling frescoes by Matthäus Günther, opulent Rococo stuccowork by Franz Xaver Feuchtmayer, and a gilded high altar establish the church as a premier highlight of European sacred art. In the adjoining Stiftsmuseum, visitors can admire precious liturgical vessels, Gothic panel paintings, Baroque vestments, and archaeological artefacts unearthed from ancient Veldidena.

Visit & Getting There

The Stiftskirche Wilten is open year-round during daytime hours with free admission (outside of church service times). The Stiftsmuseum and the historic state rooms can be visited from May to October on guided tours (groups upon prior arrangement). Directly across stands the magnificent Wiltener Basilika (Unserer Lieben Frau unter den vier Säulen), celebrated as one of Austria's finest Rococo churches. Getting there by public transport: from Innsbruck main station (Hauptbahnhof), easily reached via tram line 1 or the Stubaitalbahn (STB) directly to the Stift Wilten stop. By car: via the Brennerautobahn A13 (exit Innsbruck-Süd) or the A12; parking is available in the surrounding area.

Tips

The collegiate church offers step-free, barrier-free access for wheelchairs. If you plan your visit on a Sunday, you can attend the Sunday High Mass accompanied by superb church music performed by the Wiltener Sängerknaben. Combine your visit with an uphill walk to the Bergisel to explore the spectacular ski jump and the Tirol Panorama museum.
